verdict: Nvidia's revenue nearly quadrupled to a record $26.0B as Data Center sales jumped 427% on Hopper AI chips — and it kept $14.9B as profit, about 57 cents of every dollar.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: split-adjusted; $5.98 as reported before the June 2024 10-for-1 split; non-GAAP $0.61

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: AI data-center chips and networking — Hopper demand for training and running generative AI drove a 427% jump; enterprise, sovereign AI and healthcare buyers joined the cloud providers.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: GeForce graphics cards for gamers and AI PCs — RTX 40 series sales lifted revenue 18%.

segments.name: Professional Visualization
segments.note: Workstation graphics for designers and engineers; up 45% YoY.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Chips and software for cars and robots — self-driving platform sales drove an 11% rise.

segments.name: OEM and Other
segments.note: Smaller chip sales to other manufacturers; roughly flat YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Spending to design future chips and AI software.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales, marketing and day-to-day running costs.

otherDetail: Interest income $359M, plus $75M of other income, less $64M interest expense, net.
follow100Note: Data Center alone is $86.64 of every $100 Nvidia takes in. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segments are revenue by market platform, as NVIDIA reports them.

takeaways.title: Data Center exploded
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit a record $22.6B, up 427% from a year ago — about $87 of every $100 Nvidia took in — as cloud builders raced to train and run generative AI on Hopper chips.

takeaways.title: Well over half of sales became profit
takeaways.text: Net income reached $14.9B — 57 cents of every revenue dollar — because a 78.4% gross margin held while revenue nearly quadrupled.

takeaways.title: Guidance pointed higher still
takeaways.text: Nvidia guided second-quarter revenue to $28.0B and said the Blackwell platform was in full production; it also announced a ten-for-one stock split effective June 2024.
